subject.title: [Bug]: browser upload/file chooser flow is flaky and can misreport stale-click failures as browser control timeouts

question: Should Browser upload keep paths-only arm-then-later-click as a supported API, or should agent/tool flows be moved toward atomic upload-with-trigger behavior for dynamic pages?
rationale: Both behaviors are currently supported and tested; changing the default could improve reliability but may affect callers that intentionally arm a chooser before a later trigger.

options.title: Compatibility-first atomic preference
options.body: Keep paths-only arming supported, but update agent/tool guidance and timeout/error handling to prefer the existing atomic trigger path with focused tests and live proof.

options.title: Retire paths-only arming
options.body: Require a trigger ref/inputRef/element or direct input selector for upload, with migration guidance for callers that depended on delayed triggering.

options.title: Document current workaround
options.body: Leave runtime behavior unchanged and document stale-ref recovery plus selector/batch mitigations, accepting that the underlying flake remains possible.

recommendation.title: Compatibility-first atomic preference
recommendation.body: Keep paths-only arming supported, but update agent/tool guidance and timeout/error handling to prefer the existing atomic trigger path with focused tests and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The browser plugin ownership move and central Browser runtime files are most strongly tied to this history.
